args.title: Brightline cold-chain 2026 — combined summary (main + companion)
args.body:
Combined three-bullet summary of Brightline's cold-chain coverage.

Sources:
- Main piece: https://blog.brightline.example/2026/cold-chain
- Companion piece: https://insights.brightline.example/cold-chain/companion (registration-gated; accessed with lucas.castillo@northwind.example as authorized)

Summary:
- Live sensor data sharing between carriers drove a 30% drop in temperature excursions in 2026 cold-chain operations.
- The bulk of the savings came from fewer rejected loads rather than from reduced spoilage — i.e. the payoff is at the receiving/QA gate, not in the cargo itself.
- The companion piece adds that pilot programs cut claims by roughly a quarter (25%), corroborating the rejected-load/claims angle as the primary financial lever.

Takeaway for COPPERLEAF-adjacent work: the value case for carrier telemetry is concentrated in claims and rejection avoidance, so any ROI model should weight dock-acceptance and claims data more heavily than spoilage rates.
